ui.occurrence.summary.Storage: Windows reset its connection to {disk}, which stopped responding for a moment. The PC stalled meanwhile.
ui.occurrence.summary.Storage.retry: Windows repeated a disk operation on {disk}, which answered slowly. The PC stalled meanwhile.
ui.occurrence.summary.Storage.media: Windows reported bad sectors or a paging error on {disk}, which answered slowly. The PC stalled meanwhile.
ui.occurrence.summary.Storage.medium: Windows logged a disk connection reset (event 129) near the stall, but the disk readings were normal; it may not be the cause.
ui.occurrence.summary.Storage.retry.medi: Windows logged a repeated disk operation (event 153) near the stall, but the disk readings were normal; it may not be the cause.
ui.occurrence.summary.Storage.media.medi: Windows logged a bad block or a paging error (event 7 or 51) near the stall; the disk readings were normal. The disk may be failing.
ui.occurrence.summary.DiskIo: Disk {disk} was saturated and could not serve requests in time; the PC waited on it.
ui.occurrence.summary.DiskIo.hdd: An HDD loses far more speed than an SSD under many requests at once.
ui.occurrence.summary.DiskIo.who: Most data read and written: probably {app}. The figure includes data that never reaches the disk.
ui.occurrence.summary.Memory: Memory was almost full and Windows fell back on the page file on disk, which slows the PC down.
ui.occurrence.summary.Memory.maybe: Memory was almost full; Windows may have fallen back on the page file on disk, which slows the PC down.
ui.occurrence.summary.Cpu: The CPU was maxed out: every core busy at once.
ui.occurrence.summary.Cpu.maybe: The CPU was maxed out (every core busy at once), which may be what slowed the PC.
ui.occurrence.summary.Driver: A driver held one CPU core too long (DPC/ISR latency), and the rest of the PC waited.
ui.occurrence.summary.Driver.maybe: A driver may have held one CPU core too long (DPC/ISR latency), and the rest of the PC may have waited.
ui.occurrence.summary.GpuDriver: The graphics driver stopped responding and Windows restarted it (TDR). The picture freezes without closing programs.
ui.occurrence.summary.Throttling: The CPU ran below its normal speed because of a power or thermal limit.
ui.occurrence.summary.Throttling.maybe: The CPU may have run below its normal speed because of a power or thermal limit.
ui.occurrence.summary.App: The PC did not freeze: only {app} stopped responding. When one program hangs, the problem is usually in that program.
ui.occurrence.summary.Unclear: None of the limits Vestigium uses was crossed; the cause was not identified.
ui.occurrence.summary.BlueScreen: Windows stopped with a blue screen (code {code}) and restarted. The usual causes are a driver, memory or overheating.
ui.occurrence.summary.Unresponsive: The PC stopped responding and was turned off with the power button. What ran before is the main clue.
ui.occurrence.summary.SleepTransition: Unexpected shutdown while going to sleep, hibernating or waking. The usual cause is a driver that mishandles sleep.
ui.occurrence.summary.PowerCut: Windows logged no cause: a power loss, a hard hang or a blue screen with no dump.
ui.occurrence.summary.PowerCut.no_dump: Windows had already warned it could not prepare a crash dump; a blue screen would leave no record.
ui.occurrence.summary.HardwareFault: The hardware logged a fatal error (WHEA) just before the shutdown: CPU, memory or a slot.
ui.occurrence.summary.NotMeasured: Vestigium has no readings for this moment, so it cannot say what happened.
ui.occurrence.note.Driver: A capture of a few minutes identifies the driver. Start it while the stutters happen.
ui.occurrence.note.default: A capture of a few minutes can identify the cause. Start it while the problem happens.
ui.occurrence.ev.DiskActivePct.over: Disk {subject} busy almost all the time
ui.occurrence.ev.CoreDpcIsrPct.over: A driver held {subject} of the CPU too long
ui.occurrence.ev.process.IoBytesPerS.pla: Most data read and written: probably {app}

ui.occurrence.ev.hang.tech: IsHungAppWindow true for {duration} (Windows marks it after 5 s)

ui.occurrence.event.BugCheck: Windows restarted after a blue screen
ui.occurrence.event.CpuFirmwareLimit: The firmware limited the CPU speed

ui.occurrence.todo.none: No action suggested for this cause. If it repeats, check resource usage in Now.
ui.occurrence.dump.title: Dump of this shutdown
ui.occurrence.step.UpdateStorageDriver: Update the disk controller driver (SATA or NVMe) from the PC or motherboard maker's website.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckDiskCable: On a desktop, swap the SATA cable or the disk's port on the motherboard.
ui.occurrence.step.RunDiskTest: Run the surface scan in Tests to find unreadable sectors.
ui.occurrence.step.FindDiskHeavyApp: If it repeats, check in Now what is using the disk and pause what can wait.
ui.occurrence.step.CloseMemoryHeavyApp: Close unused programs and tabs to free memory.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckCooling: Check that the vents are clear and the fans work; clean out the dust.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckPowerPlan: On a laptop, plug in and use the best performance power mode.
ui.occurrence.step.UpdateGpuDriver: Update the graphics driver from the maker's website or app.
ui.occurrence.step.EnableSensitiveMode: If it freezes again, turn on sensitive mode from the tray: for 30 minutes monitoring is more detailed.
ui.occurrence.step.ReportToAppVendor: If it repeats, update or reinstall {app}; if it persists, report it to the developer.

ui.occurrence.step.UpdateDriver: Update the driver {driver} from its maker's website or Windows Update.
ui.occurrence.step.UpdateDriver.any: Update the graphics and chipset drivers from the website of your PC or motherboard maker, or through Windows Update.
ui.occurrence.step.BackUpNow: Back up the important files on {disk} to another disk or the cloud today.
ui.occurrence.step.BackUpNow.any: Back up important files to another disk or the cloud today.
ui.occurrence.step.ReplaceDisk: Replace {disk}. Until then, avoid writing new data to it.
ui.occurrence.step.ReplaceDisk.any: Replace the disk. Until then, avoid writing new data to it.
ui.occurrence.step.FreeDiskSpace: To free up space on {disk}, use Settings › System › Storage › Cleanup recommendations or move large videos and downloads to another disk.
ui.occurrence.step.FreeDiskSpace.any: To free up space, use Settings › System › Storage › Cleanup recommendations or move large videos and downloads to another disk.
ui.occurrence.step.LetWindowsManagePageF: In System Properties › Advanced › Performance › Virtual memory, let Windows manage the page file size.
ui.occurrence.step.CheckHardwareStabilit: Undo any CPU, memory or GPU overclock and check the temperatures.
ui.occurrence.step.ReadCrashDump: Open Dumps to read the crash dump; it shows what Windows blamed.
ui.occurrence.step.KeepOneAntivirus: Keep only one antivirus: uninstall the one you do not need.
ui.occurrence.step.ReviewStartupApps: Turn off the startup apps you do not use (Task Manager › Startup apps).
ui.occurrence.step.WaitForShutdown: Wait for the screen and the PC's LEDs to go off before cutting power.
ui.occurrence.step.MoveWindowsToSsd: If possible, put Windows on an SSD: it is the upgrade with the biggest impact.

ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.why.Critical: The disk's SMART predicts failure. Files still open, but that can change at any time. Back up now.
ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.why.Attention: The disk reallocated damaged sectors to its spare area or logged uncorrectable errors. A growing count of reallocated sectors means wear.
ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.why.Hot: The NVMe disk reported a temperature outside its safe range. This usually passes once it cools down; it does not mean the disk is failing.
ui.health.kind.DiskSmart.rule: Critical with PredictFailure, an NVMe critical warning other than temperature or spare below its threshold. Attention with the NVMe temperature warning alone, SMART 5, 187, 188, 197 or 198 above 0, NVMe use at 90% or more, or NVMe media errors.
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.title.Atten: Windows reset or retried operations on a disk
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.tech: Disk errors in the System log, 30 days
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.why.Critica: Windows logged unreadable sectors on a disk. Files in those sectors may be corrupted.
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.why.Attenti: Windows lost contact with a disk for a moment and reset the connection or retried the operation. Common causes: the controller driver or the cable.
ui.health.kind.StorageErrors.rule: Critical with a bad-block or paging error in 30 days. Attention with a storage reset or a retried disk operation in 30 days.
ui.health.kind.LowSpace.title: Low free space on the Windows disk ({subject})
ui.health.kind.LowSpace.why: Below 10% free, Windows has little room for updates and for the page file to grow.
ui.health.kind.LowSpace.rule: Attention below 10% free; critical below 5% or 5 GB. Closes above 12%.
ui.health.kind.WindowsOnHdd.title: Windows installed on an HDD
ui.health.kind.WindowsOnHdd.why: An HDD is much slower than an SSD under simultaneous access, which Windows does all the time.
ui.health.kind.WindowsOnHdd.rule: Attention when the disk that holds the Windows folder has a seek penalty (HDD).
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.why.Critica: Windows stopped with a blue screen this week. One can be isolated; several point to a driver, memory or overheating.
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.why.Attenti: The PC shut down while in use more than once this month: a power loss, the power button held down, or a hang with nothing logged.
ui.health.kind.DirtyRestarts.rule: Attention with 2 or more Kernel-Power 41 outside shutdown in 30 days; critical with a bug check in 7 days.
ui.health.kind.ShutdownUnfinished.title: Shutdown interrupted
ui.health.kind.ShutdownUnfinished.why: The PC stopped before it finished shutting down: a power cut, a hang, or something holding up the shutdown. It is not a shutdown while in use.
ui.health.kind.ShutdownUnfinished.rule: Attention with 2 or more Kernel-Power 41 whose SleepInProgress is 6 (shutting down) in 30 days.
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.title: More failures than usual this week
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.tech: Failures in 7 days against the weekly average of the 4 weeks before
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.why: Windows logged at least twice as many failures this week (programs that crashed, unexpected shutdowns, hangs) as in a normal week before.
ui.health.kind.FailuresRising.rule: Attention with 3 or more failures in 7 days and at least twice the weekly average of the 4 weeks before.
ui.health.kind.NoCrashDump.title: Blue screen dumps effectively off
ui.health.kind.NoCrashDump.why: Windows could not prepare the blue screen dump, usually because the page file is off or too small. A blue screen would leave no record.
ui.health.kind.NoCrashDump.rule: Attention with volmgr 46 (crash dump initialization failed) in 30 days.
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.title: Memory often maxed out
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.tech: Memory in use above 85%, days of the last 7
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.why: On several days this week memory use went above 85% and Windows fell back on the page file, which slows the PC down.
ui.health.kind.MemoryOften.rule: Attention with 3 of the last 7 days above 85% memory in use; closes at 1 day or fewer.
ui.health.kind.PageFile.tech: Page file and commit charge, 7 days
ui.health.kind.PageFile.why.Critical: This week memory commit came close to the limit (RAM + page file). Above it, programs fail or close.
ui.health.kind.PageFile.why.Attention: Without a page file, memory has no headroom to grow, and a blue screen leaves no dump.
ui.health.kind.PageFile.rule: Critical with a commit peak of 90% of the limit or more in 7 days, or Resource-Exhaustion 2004; attention with no page file. Closes below 80%.
ui.health.kind.SlowBoot.title: Slow startup
ui.health.kind.SlowBoot.why: Windows measured the startup time and some phases took longer than normal.
ui.health.kind.SlowBoot.rule: Attention when the last startup took more than 90 s or Windows flagged a slow step in 30 days; healthy up to 60 s.
ui.health.kind.HardwareErrors.why: The CPU, memory or a slot reported an error to Windows. Corrected errors can precede failures; a fatal one takes the PC down.
ui.health.kind.HardwareErrors.rule: Attention with any WHEA-Logger error in 30 days; critical when one is fatal (WHEA-Logger 18).
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.title: Graphics driver restarting often
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.why: When the GPU stops responding, Windows restarts its driver (TDR): the screen blinks or freezes for a moment. Twice or more in a week calls for action.
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.rule: Attention with 2 or more Display 4101 in 7 days; critical with 5 or more.
ui.health.kind.DisplayResets.count.zero: no graphics driver restart in 7 days
ui.health.kind.Throttling.title: CPU throttling
ui.health.kind.Throttling.why: The firmware limited the CPU speed, usually because of temperature or the power plan. The PC is slower while it lasts.
ui.health.kind.Throttling.rule: Attention with any Kernel-Processor-Power 37 in 7 days.
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.title: Two antivirus programs active
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.tech: Windows Security Center: real-time products on
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.why: Two antivirus programs with real-time protection interfere with each other and slow the PC down without adding security.
ui.health.kind.TwoAntivirus.rule: Attention with 2 or more antivirus products on in Windows Security Center.

ui.tweaks.what.FastStartup: At shutdown, Windows hibernates the kernel to start faster. On some PCs that shutdown never finishes.
ui.tweaks.what.FastStartup.tech: Fast Startup: at shutdown the kernel and drivers go to hiberfil.sys (hybrid boot).
ui.tweaks.what.Hibernation: Saves memory to a file (hiberfil.sys) to hibernate; the file takes a good share of the RAM size.
ui.tweaks.what.Hibernation.tech: hiberfil.sys on the system drive; turned off through SystemReserveHiberFile.
ui.tweaks.what.PowerPlan: The Power saver plan slows the CPU to save energy, which a PC on mains power does not need.
ui.tweaks.what.PowerPlan.tech: Active scheme Power saver to Balanced, through PowerSetActiveScheme.
ui.tweaks.what.PcieAspm: Briefly powers down the PCIe link to the disk and network to save energy. On some motherboards it causes stutters.
ui.tweaks.what.PcieAspm.tech: Link State Power Management of the active scheme, plugged-in value.
ui.tweaks.what.UsbSuspend: Powers down idle USB ports to save energy. Some devices are slow to come back.
ui.tweaks.what.UsbSuspend.tech: USB selective suspend of the active scheme, plugged-in value.
ui.tweaks.what.SysMain: Preloads the most used programs into memory (Superfetch). On an HDD it keeps the disk busy.
ui.tweaks.what.SysMain.tech: SysMain: prefetching and memory compression; on a hard disk it reads the system disk at random.
ui.tweaks.what.WindowsSearch.tech: WSearch service with SearchIndexer.exe and its helpers.
ui.tweaks.what.GameDvr: Continuously records the last minutes of a game so a clip can be saved later. Uses the GPU and disk.
ui.tweaks.what.GameDvr.tech: Xbox Game Bar background capture: constant video encoding while a game runs.
ui.tweaks.what.GpuScheduling: The GPU manages its own work queue. On some PCs it helps, on others it causes stutters.
ui.tweaks.what.GpuScheduling.tech: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, HwSchMode 2 on and 1 off.
ui.tweaks.what.Mpo: A Windows feature to display video and games with less processing. With two monitors it can cause flicker or stutters.
ui.tweaks.what.Mpo.tech: Multiplane overlay, turned off by OverlayTestMode = 5.
ui.tweaks.what.StartupApp: Startup app: opens automatically at sign-in.
ui.tweaks.what.StartupApp.tech: Run entry turned off through Explorer's StartupApproved, as Task Manager does.
ui.tweaks.what.AppDumps: When an app crashes, Windows saves a minidump, which the Dumps page reads.
ui.tweaks.what.AppDumps.tech: Creates the WER LocalDumps key with DumpType 1 (minidump) and DumpCount 10.
ui.tweaks.what.CrashDump: Sets the dump Windows writes on a blue screen.
ui.tweaks.risk.FastStartup: Startup takes a few seconds longer.
ui.tweaks.risk.Hibernation: Also turns off fast startup and the option to hibernate.
ui.tweaks.risk.PcieAspm: Plugged in, slightly higher power use.
ui.tweaks.risk.UsbSuspend: Plugged in, slightly higher power use.
ui.tweaks.risk.SysMain: Frequently used programs may open a little slower.
ui.tweaks.risk.GameDvr: Recording the last minutes stops working.
ui.tweaks.risk.GpuScheduling: Some games run better with it on; the change can be undone.
ui.tweaks.risk.Mpo: Usually no effect outside flicker cases.
ui.tweaks.risk.StartupApp: Nothing is deleted: the app still opens manually and can be turned back on here.
ui.tweaks.risk.AppDumps: Each dump takes a few MB.
ui.tweaks.risk.CrashDump: A complete dump can take as much disk space as the RAM.
ui.tweaks.why_not.FastStartup: No interrupted shutdowns in 30 days and no Health alert about it.
ui.tweaks.why_not.Hibernation: Enough space on the system drive.
ui.tweaks.why_not.PowerPlan: The PC is not on the Power saver plan, or it is on battery.
ui.tweaks.why_not.PcieAspm: No capture pointed at a disk or network driver.
ui.tweaks.why_not.UsbSuspend: No capture pointed at a USB driver.
ui.tweaks.why_not.SysMain: Windows is not on an HDD, or the system disk was not saturated for long.
ui.tweaks.why_not.WindowsSearch: Indexing never showed up as the cause of an overloaded disk or CPU.
ui.tweaks.why_not.GameDvr: Background recording is off, or there were few stutters this week.
ui.tweaks.why_not.GpuScheduling: No graphics driver restarts and no report pointed at the graphics driver.
ui.tweaks.why_not.Mpo: The PC has one monitor, or there were no graphics driver restarts or stutters.
ui.tweaks.why_not.StartupApp: Did not delay startup in the last full scan.
ui.tweaks.why_not.CrashDump: Windows already writes a dump on a blue screen.
ui.tweaks.signal.dumps_off: Windows is set to write no dump on a blue screen

ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.title: Memory test error
ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.tech: Windows Memory Diagnostic and the quick test
ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.why: A memory test read back a different value from the one written. That causes program crashes, corrupted files and shutdowns with no clear cause.
ui.health.kind.MemoryTestErrors.rule: Critical with MemoryDiagnostics-Results 1102 or 1202, or a quick test with errors in 90 days, until a clean Windows diagnostic comes after them.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.title.Atte: Very slow reads in regions of {subject}
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.why.Critic: The surface scan found unreadable sectors. Data in those sectors may be lost, and the damage tends to grow.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.why.Attent: On an HDD, blocks over 500 ms on two reads in a row mark areas the disk struggles to read.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.rule: Critical with any unreadable sector in the last surface scan; attention with 10 or more HDD blocks of 500 ms or more, read twice, when no other program was using the disk. A later clean scan closes it.
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.count.one: {count} region with unreadable or slow sectors
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.count.othe: {count} regions with unreadable or slow sectors
ui.health.kind.DiskUnreadable.count.zero: no region with unreadable or slow sectors
ui.health.kind.VolumeErrors.title: File system errors on {subject}
ui.health.kind.VolumeErrors.why: chkdsk found inconsistencies in this volume's file system. Windows fixes them at a restart; until then, a corrupted file may not open.
ui.health.kind.VolumeErrors.rule: Attention when the last chkdsk /scan of the volume found problems; a later clean check closes it.
ui.occurrence.step.RunMemoryDiagnostic: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic from Tests; it runs at the next restart.

ui.detail.diag.what: The Windows Memory Diagnostic restarts the PC and tests the memory outside Windows. It is the most thorough memory test and the slowest.
ui.detail.diag.step.save: Save your work often: memory errors corrupt files and cause blue screens.
ui.detail.diag.step.swap: Test one memory module at a time to find the faulty one; a faulty module has to be replaced.
ui.detail.diag.gone: Windows keeps these results in its System log, and this run has already left it.
ui.detail.quick.clean: Every word read back as written.
ui.detail.surface.outside: Other programs were using this disk during the scan, so slow reads may not be the disk's fault. Run it again with the PC idle.
ui.detail.bench.outside: Other programs used the disk meanwhile, so the numbers may be low.
ui.detail.driver.note: The longest call is the worst single time the driver held the CPU; it is not the driver's total time.
ui.detail.driver.no_calls: This capture kept no single call of this driver.
ui.detail.smart.title: SMART attribute
ui.detail.smart.watched: Vestigium monitors this attribute: a raw value above zero is a sign of a failing disk.
ui.detail.smart.plain: The disk reports this value for its maker's own use; Vestigium does not raise an alert for it.
ui.detail.smart.normalized: The disk also rates it {current} on its own scale, {worst} at its worst.
ui.detail.smart.days_none: Vestigium keeps one reading a day; the line appears from the second day.
ui.detail.smart.step: Keep an eye on this value over the next days; if it rises, back up your files and test the disk.
ui.detail.smart.unread: SMART has not been read for this disk yet. Read it from the disk's tests.
